outcomeNote: Measurement contribution that also refuted the premise it was built to test.
changedBeliefs: Exp 245/246 showed transfer is only 6-12% of a large select and left the other ~90% labelled SQLite stepping plus Dart object-graph build. Exp 251 decomposes that residual with the real resqliteStepRow/executeQuery paths in a native-asset-aware AOT harness across five fresh processes and four representative integer, mixed, and text shapes.

The direct worker-path full proxy is typically 84-94% of separately measured main-observed select() latency, but it contains no universal dominant sub-cost: the mixed row is result-construction-heavy (63%), the small integer row is step-heavy (60%), and the two other shapes are roughly even. Estimated result construction is 34-58% of observed latency, so the residual bucket is not itself an optimization candidate and a broad decode/storage rewrite cannot cite general decode dominance.

Exp 258's 60-90% synthetic no-boxing build win is real but only applies to a shape-dependent slice of the real path. Exp 251 strengthens exp 258's rejection of the broad columnar store without closing its narrow positive result: main-isolate integer consume can still benefit from Int64List locality, but this worker-side decomposition supplies no downstream incidence for an integer-heavy main-isolate-bound workload.
nextSignals: Do not reopen a general ResultSet backing-store or decode rewrite from the statement that transfer leaves ~90% of select wall. First run benchmark/experiments/step_vs_decode.dart on the representative workload and name whether stepping, value materialization, transfer, or main-isolate consumption is actually eligible.

The exp 258 narrow integer-column candidate remains blocked on a downstream workload profile showing integer-heavy, main-isolate-bound full consumption. Exp 251 is a worker-side decomposition and does not satisfy that incidence gate.
Keep the AOT native-asset bundle and fresh-process protocol when using this harness. A standalone dart compile exe does not bundle resqlite's native asset and is not a valid measurement surface.

claims.text: Across five AOT process runs, a direct-handle step-only reference found no universal dominant worker-path bucket: estimated decode/result construction was 49%, 63%, 40%, and 51% of full query/decode wall for 10k x 20 INTEGER, 10k mixed, 5k x 4 INTEGER, and 5k TEXT shapes. The full worker-path proxy was typically 91%, 92%, 84%, and 94% of separately measured main-observed Database.select() latency.
claims.conditions: Apple M-series · arm64 macOS · Dart 3.12.2 · AOT CLI native-asset bundle · five fresh processes · 2026-08

claims.text: The post-transfer large-read residual is shape-dependent rather than a single Dart-decode bottleneck, so it does not justify a broad ResultSet storage rewrite; a future candidate must first establish a workload-specific eligible phase against public select() wall.
claims.conditions: INTEGER, mixed INTEGER/TEXT, and long-TEXT result shapes · AOT · 2026-08
